audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL JSON-RPC filter processing (EIP-234), EOF metadata sections (EIP-7834), Byzantium state transitions and PoW consensus, bloom filter construction (Prague), SELFDESTRUCT deprecation (EIP-6049), SSTORE gas metering (EIP-1283), uncle block RPC responses (EIP-3046), wallet chain switching (EIP-3326), RIPEMD-160 precompile (Cancun), and CL P2P gossip/sync protocols (Gloas).

out_of_scope: Full EVM opcode implementation beyond SSTORE/SELFDESTRUCT
Full beacon state transition beyond Gloas P2P scope

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed filter requests with invalid blockHash, resource exhaustion via repeated filter queries, trick users into switching to malicious chains, exploit SSTORE gas metering for cheaper-than-expected storage manipulation
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with incorrect PoW/difficulty, submit blocks with manipulated bloom filters, exploit uncle block processing
Deploy EOF containers with crafted metadata to mislead verification tools, exploit SELFDESTRUCT semantics before deprecation takes effect

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid beacon blocks, submit conflicting attestations, broadcast fake proposer preferences to redirect execution payments
Submit fraudulent execution payload bids, publish invalid payload envelopes, attempt to circumvent solvency checks
Provide incorrect sync data, withhold blocks to slow sync, send oversized responses

misclassified_entities.reason: Transaction Execution Engine is an internal EL component (the EVM), not an external entity. Log entries are produced internally during contract execution.
A calling contract invoking a precompile is an internal EVM operation. The contract runs within the EVM execution context and is not external to the system.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Log Filtering)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_getLogs / eth_newFilter RPC with blockHash parameter
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public JSON-RPC endpoint, no authentication required. User can submit arbitrary blockHash values, malformed filter parameters, or conflicting fromBlock/toBlock with blockHash.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Uncle Queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public JSON-RPC endpoint. User can query arbitrary block numbers and uncle indices. Response must correctly include/exclude baseFee based on fork status.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Bloom Filter Search)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Public RPC endpoint. Bloom filters are used to optimize search, but an attacker could craft queries to trigger worst-case bloom false positives, causing full log scans.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (Block Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer. Can send blocks with invalid headers, incorrect PoW, manipulated difficulty, or invalid ommer references. Full block validation including header, ommers, transactions, and root hashes is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender via Signed Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Authenticated only by ECDSA signature (proves key possession, not trustworthiness). Transaction content including gas, value, data, and nonce must be fully validated. Sender may attempt to exploit SSTORE gas metering (EIP-1283) or SELFDESTRUCT semantics.

trusted_external_entities.name: Contract Deployer via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Contract creation transaction with EOF bytecode
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone can deploy contracts. EOF container validation must enforce metadata section size range (1-65535), correct section ordering, and structural integrity. Malicious deployers may craft metadata to mislead verification tools.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via wallet_switchEthereumChain
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Untrusted web application requesting chain switch. May attempt to trick user into switching to a malicious chain, probe wallet capabilities for fingerprinting, or disrupt pending operations by triggering chain switches.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Miner via PoW
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Block header with nonce/mixDigest for PoW verification
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Miner identity is established only through valid PoW. Miner can attempt to manipulate difficulty, include invalid ommers for extra rewards, or exploit the bomb delay calculation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Beacon Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer. Can forward invalid beacon blocks, attempt to flood gossip with invalid messages. All gossip messages require proposer index, signature, and slot timing validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Payload Builder via Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Builder is authenticated on-chain via is_active_builder check and BLS signature, but bid content (payment amount, fee_recipient, gas_limit) must be fully validated against proposer preferences and builder solvency (can_builder_cover_bid). Builder may attempt to submit underfunded bids or mismatched preferences.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Proposer is authenticated via BLS signature and slot assignment verification, but preferences content must still be validated. A compromised validator key could broadcast conflicting preferences.

trusted_external_entities.name: Sync Peer via Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: BeaconBlocksByRange v2, BeaconBlocksByRoot v2, ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRange v1, ExecutionPayloadEnvelopesByRoot v1
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peer responding to sync requests. May provide incorrect data, omit blocks, or send responses that don't match request parameters. All received data must be validated against request parameters and structural checks.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full parameter validation required: blockHash format (valid 32-byte hex), mutual exclusivity with fromBlock/toBlock, block existence verification. Must handle non-existent block hashes gracefully with error code -32000.
Must validate block number and uncle index parameters. Must correctly determine EIP-1559 fork status to include/exclude baseFee field. Must handle non-existent uncles gracefully.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: eth_getLogs RPC with bloom filter optimization
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Bloom filter search must handle worst-case false positive rates. Query parameters (address, topics) must be validated. Resource limits should prevent unbounded log scanning.

Full block validation required: header validation (sequential numbering, timestamp, gas limit, difficulty, parent hash), ommer validation (max 2, no duplicates, age 1-6, valid ancestry), transaction execution, and root hash verification (state root, tx root, receipt root, logs bloom).

Full transaction validation: ECDSA signature recovery, nonce match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender is EOA, intrinsic gas check, available gas check. SSTORE operations must be correctly metered per EIP-1283 three-value tracking. Refund counter must be capped at 50% of gas consumed.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: EOF container validation during contract deployment
boundary_edges.security_assumption: EOF structural validation required: header parsing, metadata marker (0x05) detection, metadata size range (1-65535), section position ordering (metadata before data). Invalid containers must be rejected. Metadata content is opaque and not validated at protocol level.

Must validate chainId hex format (EIP-695), verify chain exists in wallet registry, confirm wallet can service target chain. Must display requester identity and target chain to user for informed consent. Must mitigate fingerprinting via chain probing. Must cancel pending requests/confirmations on chain switch.

SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated (EIP-6049). Current semantics transfer balance to beneficiary and mark contract for removal. Future breaking changes expected. Implementations must handle current semantics correctly while preparing for deprecation.

Must verify PoW result <= 2^256/difficulty. Difficulty calculation must correctly apply bomb delay (subtract 3M blocks). Block reward must be exactly 3 ETH (Byzantium). Ommer rewards must follow formula ((8 - age) * 3 ETH) / 8.
Must validate proposer index, BLS signature, slot timing. Execution payload validations are replaced with bid-based checks in Gloas fork.
Must verify builder is active via is_active_builder, payment > 0, fee_recipient and gas_limit match proposer preferences, builder can cover bid via can_builder_cover_bid. BLS signature must be valid.
Must verify builder BLS signature, block root matches known block, payload matches bid. KZG commitments relocated to bid message must be correctly validated.
Must verify proposer is assigned to declared slot in next epoch. BLS signature validation required. Preferences must be well-formed with valid fee_recipient, gas_limit, and slot assignment.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Req/Resp sync protocol (blocks and payload envelopes)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Responses must match request parameters (start_slot, count, requested roots). Response size limited to MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB. All received blocks and envelopes must pass structural validation before integration into local database.
